title: Inclusive education
introduction: Study and design of educational approaches and tools combining extended reality (VR and AR) and artificial intelligence to train teachers to better support learners with disabilities.

highlights.label: Inclusive education
highlights.value: Creation of educational content to train educators to better support learners with disabilities.

highlights.label: Extended reality
highlights.value: Use of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) to create immersive educational scenarios.

highlights.label: Artificial intelligence
highlights.value: Use of generative AI to create applications that respond naturally to user actions.

paragraphs: During my contract at I-MAGINEXR, I was responsible for supervising a CIFRE PhD student whose research focused on the use of virtual reality (VR) and generative artificial intelligence (AI) to improve teacher training in supporting learners with disabilities, particularly those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). The supervision of this PhD formed part of a collaboration with Karine GALMICHE, also at I-MAGINEXR, Simon RICHIR and Sylvain FLEURY (ENSAM), and Nour EL-MAWAS (Université de Lorraine).

By applying a design-based research methodology, we first studied the current needs of teachers, particularly those who had already completed training on supporting learners with disabilities or had previously supported at least one learner with ASD. Through questionnaires, interviews and co-design workshops, we identified these needs and designed three educational scenarios that could be integrated into an educational application.

We then began designing and developing VR applications incorporating these different scenarios. For this purpose, we used the OpenSpace3D engine developed by I-MAGINEXR, which enabled us to design the scenarios in full. As all these scenarios rely on interactions with virtual avatars representing learners, we also used generative AI to create agents playing their roles. The avatars' reactions therefore appear natural and adapt to the user's actions. Generative AI is also used at the end of the application to conduct a debriefing with the user and allow them to assess their performance during the scenario.
At present, two scientific papers are being written on this research theme, and work on the VR application is continuing.
